title: Prefetch cost sensitivity sketch notes
content:
Context and goal

Goal: sketch a lightweight adaptive prefetch controller that trades off extra token cost vs tail-latency and cold-start miss rate. This is personal notes — exploratory, rough math, candidate API shapes and experiments.

Why: we see cases where prefix caching and speculative prefetch reduce latency but can double token cost on low-value requests. Need a signal-driven policy that respects a per-customer budget and per-route latency SLOs.

High level idea
- Keep prefetch decision scoped to request context and a short-term budget window (eg per-minute token budget).
- Score prefetch candidate by expected latency reduction * value_weight - expected token_cost * cost_weight.
- Value weight can be simple proxies: is_interactive, is_billing_user, route_priority, client-predicted-latency-urgency.
- Budget throttle: soft budget + emergency fallback (no prefetch when spent).

Signals to use (cheap):
- recent_cache_hit_rate (prefix/KV hits) over last N calls
- average_inflight_batch_size and queue length
- observed_tail_latencies (p95) per route
- token_cost_estimate for model/variant at length L
- request_type labels: interactive | background | embed-update

Simple scoring function (proto)
score = latency_reduction_estimate * V - token_cost_estimate * C - risk_penalty
where
- latency_reduction_estimate approximated by: base_infer_latency(model, seq_len) - cached_kv_latency_estimate
- token_cost_estimate = tokens_prefetched * unit_cost(model_variant)
- V, C are tunable scalars at route or customer level

Prefetch policy API sketch (config + runtime hooks)
- config prefetch_policy:
  enabled: true
  mode: adaptive   # adaptive | aggressive | disabled
  budget_tokens_per_min: 15000
  max_prefetch_tokens_per_req: 1024
  target_p95_ms: 120
  value_weights:
    interactive: 1.0
    background: 0.2
    high_priority_route: 1.5
  cost_weight: 0.001  # scaled so cost and latency are comparable
  risk_penalty_base: 0.1
  cooldown_seconds_after_budget_spendout: 60

Runtime hook points (cheap and local):
- on_request_start(context): fetch recent small-window stats for route/customer
- score_prefix_candidates(candidate_list): returns sorted candidates with score
- apply_prefetch(candidate): enqueue speculative request to model variant with prefetch flag
- on_prefetch_result(callback): attach TTL / eviction policy into KV cache

Example candidate selection pseudocode
1) enumerate candidates: next_n_tokens for prefixes used by route heuristics (eg 32, 64, 128)
2) for each candidate compute token_cost_est, lat_red_est, score
3) filter by max_prefetch_tokens_per_req and budget left in sliding window
4) pick top candidate where score > threshold or mode == aggressive

Edge cases and safety
- Never prefetch when request contains sensitive markers unless customer opt-in
- If budget exhausted, still allow a tiny emergency prefetch for small latency-sensitive requests (configurable tiny token cap)
- If underlying model changes (variant swap), invalidate predictions and back to conservative defaults for N minutes

Experiments to run (quick sims)
- Micro-sim: synthetic arrival process with p(cache_hit)=x, latency distributions, compute cost delta and tail-latency improvements over 1k runs
- A/B: route-level rollout where 10% of traffic uses adaptive prefetch with low budget, compare token usage per session and p95 improvement
- Failure modes: bursty traffic where prefetch amplifies queueing; detect by correlating prefetch rate with enqueue length and throttle further

Metrics to track
- prefetch_tokens_per_min per-customer and per-route
- p95 latency before and after prefetch
- cache_hit_rate for prefetched prefixes
- token_cost_delta and cost per ms improvement ratio

Open questions / TODOs
- How to estimate latency_reduction for multi-variant fleets without heavy instrumentation? Proposal: use recent median per-variant latency and model scaled factor for KV fast-path
- How to represent customer-level budgets in existing billing model? likely on top of tokens, separate prefetch counter with opt-in
- Do we need model-aware cost weights for quantized variants? yes, unit_cost should include quantization factor
- Integrate with routing policies: if lowest-cost fallback is used, prefetch decisions should prefer cheaper variant if latency benefit still acceptable

Quick ascii diagram of flow
client -> router -> prefetch controller -> (score) -> prefetch enqueue -> model shard
                            |                                          |
                            |-- no prefetch -> normal infer  <--------|

Notes to self: keep this as minimal runtime logic runnable in edge proxies or local request proxy (small microservice). Avoid heavy ML models for scoring. Start with deterministic scoring and coarse tuning knobs, iterate with telemetry.

Small config example for dev testing
experiment: prefetch-low-budget
routes:
  /chat/stream:
    prefetch_policy:
      enabled: true
      mode: adaptive
      budget_tokens_per_min: 3000
      max_prefetch_tokens_per_req: 128
      target_p95_ms: 150

Next steps
- write micro-sim in notebook: simulate 3 traffic shapes, 2 cache hit regimes, 3 budget profiles
- instrument a lightweight telemetry event for prefetch decisions (reason, candidate_size, score, budget_left)
- sync with billing to prototype prefetch counters for one dev account

End of scratchpad.
